[Doctor]: Good morning, Mr. Lee. How are you doing today?

[Patient]: Good morning, doctor. I'm really struggling with this shoulder pain.

[Doctor]: I'm sorry to hear that, Mr. Lee. Can you tell me more about this pain?

[Patient]: Sure, doc. The pain is in my right shoulder, and it has been really bad for about 6 weeks now. It's continuous and gets worse at night. I can't even lift my arm, which is making my job and daily life really difficult.

[Doctor]: That sounds very uncomfortable. Have you had any similar issues before?

[Patient]: No, this is the first time my shoulder has been this bad. But I do have chronic lower back pain.

[Doctor]: I see. Are you currently taking any prescription medications for your back pain or any other condition?

[Patient]: No, I'm not on any prescription medications right now.

[Doctor]: Okay, let me take a thorough look at your shoulder. But first, let's review some other aspects of your health. Any numbness or tingling in your arm or hand?

[Patient]: No, I haven't felt any numbness or tingling.

[Doctor]: And how has your sleep been affected by the shoulder pain?

[Patient]: It's been terrible. The pain wakes me up multiple times at night.

[Doctor]: I can understand how frustrating that must be. Have you experienced any recent weight loss or fever?

[Patient]: No, none of that.

[Doctor]: Alright, let's examine your shoulder. Please have a seat. I'll start by looking at your general appearance and taking your vital signs, which seem to be within normal limits.

[Patient]: Okay, doctor.

[Doctor]: Now, I'm going to inspect your right shoulder. I see some swelling and bruising. Does it hurt when I touch here?

[Patient]: Yes, that's very tender.

[Doctor]: I understand. Let's check your range of motion. Can you try to lift your arm for me?

[Patient]: (Attempts to lift arm) I can't lift it very high. It's really painful.

[Doctor]: I see. You have severely limited range of motion, especially in abduction and external rotation. How about your strength in the shoulder?

[Patient]: It's quite weak. I can't really use it for anything heavy.

[Doctor]: Alright, Mr. Lee. From what I've observed, it looks like you might have a rotator cuff tear. We'll need to do some further investigations to confirm this.

[Patient]: Oh, no. What does that mean?

[Doctor]: A rotator cuff tear is when one of the tendons in your shoulder tears, causing pain and limited movement. We'll start with a corticosteroid injection for immediate pain relief and prescribe Naproxen for the inflammation.

[Patient]: But I'm allergic to NSAIDs.

[Doctor]: Thank you for reminding me. We'll discuss alternative pain management options. In addition, I will order an ultrasound of your right shoulder to assess the soft tissue damage.

[Patient]: Okay, doctor. What happens next?

[Doctor]: After the ultrasound, we'll have a follow-up appointment in about 3 weeks to review the results and see how you're responding to the treatment. Depending on the findings, we might need to consider further treatment options.

[Patient]: Like surgery?

[Doctor]: Possibly. I'll refer you to an orthopedic surgeon, Dr. John Smith, for a consultation. He can provide more information on potential surgical interventions if necessary.

[Patient]: Alright, doctor. I just want to get back to work as soon as possible.

[Doctor]: I understand, Mr. Lee. It's important to follow up regularly and adhere to the treatment plan. We'll do our best to help you recover quickly.

[Patient]: Thank you, doctor. I appreciate it.

[Doctor]: You're welcome, Mr. Lee. Let me summarize the plan: we'll start with a corticosteroid injection and an alternative pain management plan since you can't take NSAIDs. We'll also conduct an ultrasound of your shoulder, and you'll follow up in 3 weeks. I'll refer you to Dr. Smith for a potential surgical consultation.

[Patient]: Got it. I'll do whatever it takes.

[Doctor]: Great. Do you have any other questions for me?

[Patient]: No, I think that's everything for now.

[Doctor]: Alright then. I'll have my assistant schedule your ultrasound and follow-up appointment. Take care, Mr. Lee, and I'll see you in 3 weeks.

[Patient]: Thank you, doctor. I'll see you then.
